And later, they attempt mackerel fishing on Chesil Beach, close to the species' feeding peak at dusk.

programme.title: Newsnight
programme.desc: Insights and global interviews on the news stories of the day. With Victoria Derbyshire.

programme.title: The Mother of All Cons
programme.desc: In 2010, poorly 16-year-old Megan Bhari decides to launch a charity for seriously ill children. She’s battling a brain tumour, and knowing the toll illness can take, she decides to devote her life to creating fairy-tale experiences that might help children to forget, even briefly, that they’re sick. Believe in Magic becomes an immediate success. Inspired by Megan’s courage and self-sacrifice, celebrities and her beloved One Direction are more than willing to donate their time and money to the cause. And when her mother, Jean, posts news that Megan’s health has deteriorated and she needs expensive treatment in America, countless families and celebrity supporters rally around to support Meg. Together, they raise the money needed overnight. However, in an online chat, some parents whose own children have been treated for cancer abroad begin asking questions.

programme.title: Iolo's River Valleys
programme.desc: Iolo explores the stunning Dee valley, from wintering birds along the estuary to displaying black grouse on moorland, rare freshwater-pearl mussels and spawning sea trout.

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: Matt Baker and Sammi Kinghorn explore the forests of the Welsh valleys at a critical time. As spring gives way to summer, wildlife is at its most active and visitor numbers rise, but wildfires pose a growing threat. They meet the people shaping the future of these landscapes, from fire prevention and recreation to conservation and training the next generation. Meanwhile, Tom Heap heads to Devon and Cornwall to investigate the state of the UK’s seaweed farming industry.

programme.title: Expedition with Steve Backshall
programme.desc: As Saudi Arabia opens up to the outside world, miles and miles of its vast desert landscape remain completely unknown. Over 120,000 years ago, the Arabian desert was a pathway for the first human migrations out of Africa. On this expedition, Steve and the team are following in ancient footsteps to shine a light into the unknown. Joining forces with Saudi Arabian geologists Mahmoud Al-Shanti and Hala Alwagdani, Steve and ropes expert Aldo Kane head down into an unexplored volcanic underworld in search of the longest lava tube in Arabia. Geological evidence suggests that at least 400km of tunnels lie beneath the Harrat Khaybar lava field – subterranean passageways which could contain bones and artefacts from ancient civilisations. Only 25km of these lava tubes have ever been explored - until now. Steve and the team start their journey at the ancient Nabataean city of Hegra, where secrets lie waiting to be uncovered.

programme.title: Half Man
programme.desc: 2010. Niall and Ava face major life changes as Ruben struggles with his relationship. An impulsive choice between Mona and Niall has serious consequences for all involved.

programme.title: Dear England
programme.desc: After a breakthrough World Cup reignites belief, the England team return to a tournament on home turf, amidst the Covid pandemic. As the pressure to win increases, Pippa Grange questions her role. Meanwhile, Gareth tries to unite a divided country ahead of Euro 2020, where he hopes the team finally bring it home at Wembley.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Christina Trevanion visits a pub frozen in time, where last orders were called in the 1960s and everything was left untouched. In the Devon town of Buckfastleigh, the Valiant Soldier was an inn for more than two centuries and is now a museum, giving visitors a glimpse into the past. Inside the recreated interior, Christina is told about the pub’s redoubtable landlady and the custom back in the 60s of refusing service to women in the bar. In Hele, near Exeter, two teams of shoppers rush around an antiques centre with their experts, hoping to bag profitable bargains. On the red team are dad and daughter Ade and Mel, helped by Ben Cooper, and for the blues, it’s friends Martin and Mark, aided by Gary Pe. With 60 minutes on the clock, the blue team’s first stop is a shining suit of armour. Across the centre, Mel gazes into a £200 crystal ball – does it foretell a win for the reds? In Chippenham, auctioneer Tim Weeks confidently predicts a few profits for the teams, but who will go home the victor?

programme.title: Great Continental Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Before boarding his train at Budapest’s historic Nyugati station, Michael Portillo explores its sumptuous royal waiting room, built specially for the Austro-Hungarian emperor Franz Joseph I and his empress, Elizabeth. Heading south, his next destination is the country’s third city of Szeged, close to the Serbian and Romanian borders. In the city’s historic centre, he finds the magnificent Great Synagogue, built in 1902, which reflects the size and prominence of Szeged’s Jewish population at that time. Just outside the city, on the banks of the River Tisza, Michael visits a region known for producing Hungary’s favourite spice, paprika, from ground red peppers. At a fourth-generation family farm, he tries a freshly picked pepper and joins the family for a hearty paprika stew.

programme.title: Greatest Gardens with Diarmuid Gavin and Carol Klein
programme.desc: Carol Klein and Diarmuid Gavin, along with guest judge and gardening fan Fred Sirieix, continue the search to find Northern Ireland’s greatest garden. First up is Anne’s Kilcootry Barn Gardens in Fintona, with two and a half acres of mixed gardens – filled with flower beds, a vegetable garden and an apple orchard. In Omagh, the judges visit a field of dreams – 17 acres of once-barren farmland that’s been transformed by Sir Bob and Lady Rosemary, with a formal Italianate area and a large woodland, planted with wildlife in mind. Finally, it’s off to the shores of Rossglass beach, overlooking Dundrum Bay, to visit artist Bernard’s romantic rose garden. Judges Diarmuid, Carol and Fred are searching for a garden which the owners have put their heart and soul into creating. Which will they decide deserves to be the last contender for the title of Greatest Garden?

programme.title: Just One Thing
programme.desc: Can a sweet treat ever be good for you? Zoe Ball is in Birmingham, trying to tempt fitness fanatic Bilal away from sugary sweets and towards flavanol-rich dark chocolate. Chocolate may get a bad press, but the science shows that if you go over to the dark side and eat chocolate with at least 70 per cent cocoa, it could boost your heart health, improve your brain function and even reduce the risk of type 2 diabetes. A delicious upgrade with serious benefits.

programme.title: Giorraíonn Beirt Bóthar
programme.desc: Dreapann Tessa Fleming agus Cormac Ó hÁdhmaill Sliabh gCuillinn, taiscéalann siad séadchomharthaí ársa, agus foghlaimíonn siad faoin fhoráiste. Tugann Tessa agus Cormac cuairt ar a Traditional Arts Partnership ar an Mhullach Bán sula dtéann siad an seanbhealach isteach go ríocht ársa Uladh ag na Dóirsí. Críochnaíonn siad an chuid seo den turas le cluiche liathróid láimhe i gCoilleach Eanach. Tessa Fleming and Cormac Ó hÁdhmaill climb Slieve Gullion, explore ancient monuments and learn the art of foraging. They visit the Traditional Arts Partnership in Mullaghbawn before exploring the ancient gateway to the kingdom of Ulster at Dorsey, all capped off with a roadside game of handball at Cullyhanna.

In the city’s historic centre, he finds the magnificent Great Synagogue, built in 1902, which reflects the size and prominence of Szeged’s Jewish population at that time. Just outside the city, on the banks of the River Tisza, Michael visits a region known for producing Hungary’s favourite spice, paprika, from ground red peppers. At a fourth-generation family farm, he tries a freshly picked pepper and joins the family for a hearty paprika stew.

programme.title: Greatest Gardens with Diarmuid Gavin and Carol Klein
programme.desc: Carol Klein and Diarmuid Gavin, along with guest judge and gardening fan Fred Sirieix, continue the search to find Northern Ireland’s greatest garden. First up is Anne’s Kilcootry Barn Gardens in Fintona, with two and a half acres of mixed gardens – filled with flower beds, a vegetable garden and an apple orchard. In Omagh, the judges visit a field of dreams – 17 acres of once-barren farmland that’s been transformed by Sir Bob and Lady Rosemary, with a formal Italianate area and a large woodland, planted with wildlife in mind. Finally, it’s off to the shores of Rossglass beach, overlooking Dundrum Bay, to visit artist Bernard’s romantic rose garden. Judges Diarmuid, Carol and Fred are searching for a garden which the owners have put their heart and soul into creating. Which will they decide deserves to be the last contender for the title of Greatest Garden?

programme.title: Just One Thing
programme.desc: Can a sweet treat ever be good for you? Zoe Ball is in Birmingham, trying to tempt fitness fanatic Bilal away from sugary sweets and towards flavanol-rich dark chocolate. Chocolate may get a bad press, but the science shows that if you go over to the dark side and eat chocolate with at least 70 per cent cocoa, it could boost your heart health, improve your brain function and even reduce the risk of type 2 diabetes. A delicious upgrade with serious benefits.

programme.title: Great Continental Railway Journeys
programme.desc: On the last leg of his journey, Michael Portillo arrives in the historic northern city of Eger. At its famous castle, he discovers how, during the 16th century, Ottoman invaders were defeated by a vastly outnumbered Hungarian force. It‘s a victory still celebrated to this day. Nearby, in the foothills of the Bükk Mountains, one of Hungary’s wine-producing areas, Michael takes a tour of a family-owned vineyard and samples the region’s signature wine, Bull’s Blood. Continuing east, his final destination is the Puszta, Hungary's largest national park, where animals have grazed for over 2,000 years. On a vast plain with endless skies, Michael is treated to an impressive display of horsemanship by Hungarian cowboys, called csikós.

programme.title: Digging for Britain
programme.desc: Alice Roberts celebrates the biggest and best archaeological discoveries of 2018 from the north of the UK.

programme.title: Springwatch
programme.desc: Week two of Springwatch begins with another packed line-up of wildlife stories and live camera action from across the UK. Presenters Chris Packham and Michaela Strachan uncover the dramatic moments captured over the weekend by the live cameras at National Trust Crom in Northern Ireland. This programme explores the remarkable adaptations of some of Britain’s best-loved woodland birds, whilst Iolo Williams heads into the heart of London to reveal the unexpected wildlife thriving in the capital.

programme.title: Emma Barnett: Fighting Endometriosis
programme.desc: Emma Barnett shares her life-long struggle with endometriosis – a disease affecting one in ten women of reproductive age, which causes excruciating, often debilitating, pain. Inside Emma’s body, rogue cells similar to the lining of the womb mysteriously appear on other organs, creating lesions which bleed, scar and cause inflammation. There is no cure. Endometriosis is as common as diabetes but receives a fraction of the research funding. Emma travels across the UK to meet a few of the millions of women who, like her, are suffering. Through candid conversations, they reveal the extent to which endometriosis is devastating the lives of women – affecting fertility, work and loved ones.

programme.title: Giorraíonn Beirt Bóthar
programme.desc: Dreapann Tessa Fleming agus Cormac Ó hÁdhmaill Sliabh gCuillinn, taiscéalann siad séadchomharthaí ársa, agus foghlaimíonn siad faoin fhoráiste. Tugann Tessa agus Cormac cuairt ar a Traditional Arts Partnership ar an Mhullach Bán sula dtéann siad an seanbhealach isteach go ríocht ársa Uladh ag na Dóirsí. Críochnaíonn siad an chuid seo den turas le cluiche liathróid láimhe i gCoilleach Eanach. Tessa Fleming and Cormac Ó hÁdhmaill climb Slieve Gullion, explore ancient monuments and learn the art of foraging. They visit the Traditional Arts Partnership in Mullaghbawn before exploring the ancient gateway to the kingdom of Ulster at Dorsey, all capped off with a roadside game of handball at Cullyhanna.

programme.title: Newsnight
programme.desc: Insights and global interviews on the news stories of the day. With Victoria Derbyshire.

programme.title: The Mother of All Cons
programme.desc: In 2010, poorly 16-year-old Megan Bhari decides to launch a charity for seriously ill children. She’s battling a brain tumour, and knowing the toll illness can take, she decides to devote her life to creating fairy-tale experiences that might help children to forget, even briefly, that they’re sick. Believe in Magic becomes an immediate success. Inspired by Megan’s courage and self-sacrifice, celebrities and her beloved One Direction are more than willing to donate their time and money to the cause. And when her mother, Jean, posts news that Megan’s health has deteriorated and she needs expensive treatment in America, countless families and celebrity supporters rally around to support Meg. Together, they raise the money needed overnight. However, in an online chat, some parents whose own children have been treated for cancer abroad begin asking questions.

programme.title: Iolo's River Valleys
programme.desc: Iolo explores the stunning Dee valley, from wintering birds along the estuary to displaying black grouse on moorland, rare freshwater-pearl mussels and spawning sea trout.

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: Matt Baker and Sammi Kinghorn explore the forests of the Welsh valleys at a critical time. As spring gives way to summer, wildlife is at its most active and visitor numbers rise, but wildfires pose a growing threat. They meet the people shaping the future of these landscapes, from fire prevention and recreation to conservation and training the next generation. Meanwhile, Tom Heap heads to Devon and Cornwall to investigate the state of the UK’s seaweed farming industry.

programme.title: Expedition with Steve Backshall
programme.desc: As Saudi Arabia opens up to the outside world, miles and miles of its vast desert landscape remain completely unknown. Over 120,000 years ago, the Arabian desert was a pathway for the first human migrations out of Africa. On this expedition, Steve and the team are following in ancient footsteps to shine a light into the unknown. Joining forces with Saudi Arabian geologists Mahmoud Al-Shanti and Hala Alwagdani, Steve and ropes expert Aldo Kane head down into an unexplored volcanic underworld in search of the longest lava tube in Arabia. Geological evidence suggests that at least 400km of tunnels lie beneath the Harrat Khaybar lava field – subterranean passageways which could contain bones and artefacts from ancient civilisations. Only 25km of these lava tubes have ever been explored - until now. Steve and the team start their journey at the ancient Nabataean city of Hegra, where secrets lie waiting to be uncovered.

programme.title: Half Man
programme.desc: 2010. Niall and Ava face major life changes as Ruben struggles with his relationship. An impulsive choice between Mona and Niall has serious consequences for all involved.

programme.title: Dear England
programme.desc: After a breakthrough World Cup reignites belief, the England team return to a tournament on home turf, amidst the Covid pandemic. As the pressure to win increases, Pippa Grange questions her role. Meanwhile, Gareth tries to unite a divided country ahead of Euro 2020, where he hopes the team finally bring it home at Wembley.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Christina Trevanion visits a pub frozen in time, where last orders were called in the 1960s and everything was left untouched. In the Devon town of Buckfastleigh, the Valiant Soldier was an inn for more than two centuries and is now a museum, giving visitors a glimpse into the past. Inside the recreated interior, Christina is told about the pub’s redoubtable landlady and the custom back in the 60s of refusing service to women in the bar. In Hele, near Exeter, two teams of shoppers rush around an antiques centre with their experts, hoping to bag profitable bargains. On the red team are dad and daughter Ade and Mel, helped by Ben Cooper, and for the blues, it’s friends Martin and Mark, aided by Gary Pe. With 60 minutes on the clock, the blue team’s first stop is a shining suit of armour. Across the centre, Mel gazes into a £200 crystal ball – does it foretell a win for the reds? programme.title: Deadly 60
programme.desc: In this special episode of Deadly 60, Steve Backshall takes a deep dive into the fate of one of the most extraordinary, and endangered, ecosystems on our planet: coral reefs. They may cover less than one per cent of the ocean floor, but they support roughly a quarter of all marine life and are irreplaceable - yet they are in serious trouble. Steve travels to some of the world’s most celebrated reef systems, from the shallows of the Java Sea to the tropical waters of the Maldives. Along the way, he meets all the weird and wonderful creatures that call the reef home, including some of the best-camouflaged creatures and some impressive apex predators - he even gets a telling-off from a clownfish!

programme.desc: The Twirlywoos are at a stable, where they watch as a man comes and leads a horse into the stable. When the man leaves, the Twirlywoos come out to investigate. The man comes back to find that the horse has got out and puts it back in again, only for the Twirlywoos to let it out again as soon as he goes away. This continues until the Twirlywoos fly away, managing to shut the man inside the stable and the horse outside! Back in the boat, the Box comes to visit. programme.title: Hey Duggee

programme.title: Our Family
programme.desc: Today, sisters Iona and Elba make their family’s famous shortbread biscuits and throw a picnic with teddy bears! Out in the park, they play at launching rockets into the sky. But when one of the rockets lands in a stream, will the brave astronauts be able to get it back?

programme.title: My World Kitchen
programme.desc: Zahra-Rose's family is from Somalia, a country situated on the east coast of Africa. In Somalia, they have the traditional dish of nafaqo, which is boiled egg wrapped in mashed potato. This is what Zahra-Rose has chosen to make for her friends. To begin with, Zahra-Rose seasons mashed potato with salt, black pepper, flour, ground cumin, ground coriander, turmeric powder and fresh coriander. She then wraps the potato mixture around her special ingredient, hard-boiled eggs, rolls them in breadcrumbs and puts them in the oven to be cooked. Zahra-Rose also serves a fresh chilli sauce, so her friends can use it for dipping. Not only does Zahra-Rose have beautiful decorations, she also has a surprise picnic planned. Will her friends realise what her special ingredient is?

programme.title: Maddie's Do You Know?
programme.desc: Maddie visits a farm to show us how a potato harvester works - picking out and sorting the potatoes growing in the ground. She uses her special cameras to see how the machine pulls off the roots and shakes off the soil. Then we see how the potatoes are carried up a ‘potato escalator’ to be packed into huge crates. Next, she visits a cereal factory to see how wheat biscuits are made. We find out how the wheat grains are cooked and dried in an oven – Maddie uses her special slow-motion camera so that we can see how the grains are heated – they look like they are dancing! Then Maddie helps to press them into wheat biscuit shapes ready to be packed and sent to the shops.

programme.title: Dog Squad
programme.desc: When guide dog Kika has a waggy tail-related accident with a purple smoothie, she and her owner Dr Amit visit the Woofton Library of Things to borrow a carpet cleaner.

programme.title: Go Wild
programme.desc: Aneeshwar and Lizzie meet a porcupine. They see how their super sharp spines help protect these prickly characters against even the largest of predators. Next, Aneeshwar and Lizzie meet a three-banded armadillo. They try to keep track of him as he scurries quickly around his enclosure looking for his favourite food - grubs and bugs. These two animals are very different, but Aneeshwar and Lizzie discover what the unusual and extraordinary wild connection is between them.

programme.title: Waffle the Wonder Dog

programme.desc: The Twirlywoos are at a stable, where they watch as a man comes and leads a horse into the stable. When the man leaves, the Twirlywoos come out to investigate. Toodloo climbs up and slides the bolt of the door across, while the others pull the door open, letting the horse back out of the stable. The man comes back to find that the horse has got out and puts it back in again, only for the Twirlywoos to let it out again as soon as he goes away. This continues until the Twirlywoos fly away, managing to shut the man inside the stable and the horse outside! Back in the boat, the Box comes to visit. Chickedy and Chick are impatient to find out what's inside, and they jump in, only to be sprung back out again. They keep disappearing inside the Box, only to be bounced back out again, getting higher each time until they go right up in the air and Great BigHoo and Toodloo have to catch them. Toodloo has a go at jumping in the Box, but goes right through it and then throws the Box off, which lands on Great BigHoo! At this point, the Box has enough of the game, and it bounces itself back out of the boat.

programme.desc: Zahra-Rose's family is from Somalia, a country situated on the east coast of Africa. In Somalia, they have the traditional dish of nafaqo, which is boiled egg wrapped in mashed potato. This is what Zahra-Rose has chosen to make for her friends. To begin with, Zahra-Rose seasons mashed potato with salt, black pepper, flour, ground cumin, ground coriander, turmeric powder and fresh coriander. She then wraps the potato mixture around her special ingredient, hard-boiled eggs, rolls them in breadcrumbs and puts them in the oven to be cooked. Zahra-Rose also serves a fresh chilli sauce, so her friends can use it for dipping. Not only does Zahra-Rose have beautiful decorations, she also has a surprise picnic planned. Will her friends realise what her special ingredient is?

programme.title: Maddie's Do You Know?

She uses her special cameras to see how the machine pulls off the roots and shakes off the soil. Then we see how the potatoes are carried up a ‘potato escalator’ to be packed into huge crates. Next, she visits a cereal factory to see how wheat biscuits are made. We find out how the wheat grains are cooked and dried in an oven – Maddie uses her special slow-motion camera so that we can see how the grains are heated – they look like they are dancing! Then Maddie helps to press them into wheat biscuit shapes ready to be packed and sent to the shops.

programme.desc: Rafi loves bouncing on the trampoline and wishes she could do it all day. Her feet become bouncy, and it's brilliant at first, until she realises that bouncing everywhere makes simple jobs tricky. Rafi doesn’t want any help, but soon she sees that bouncing all the time isn’t as fun as she thought. With her dads' support, she realises it’s okay to ask for help. Together, they share pancakes, laughter and a big upside-down hug.

programme.title: JoJo & Gran Gran
programme.desc: When Panda's arm gets a small tear in the park, Gran Gran has a plan to head home and set up a hospital for Panda and JoJo's other toys. After stitching up Panda's arm, they decide to do a medical check-up on the other toys, including an x-ray for Hugo the dinosaur. JoJo learns that Panda's stitches are a bit like a scar on Gran Gran's arm. JoJo learns that scars don't go away, but they don't change who you are either.

programme.title: Sarah & Duck
programme.desc: Sarah and her best friend Duck embark on simple but exciting adventures, exploring the world both near and far in their own wobbly and imaginative way. When their local park is closed, Sarah and Duck try to find a suitable alternative.

programme.title: Clangers
programme.desc: Major’s spanner, Mother’s trowel, even Baby Soup Dragon’s cotton ball disappear on the same day. One moment they are there, the next moment they have disappeared! Tiny and Small search for them everywhere but with no luck. Granny decides to take their mind off the mystery by telling them a story about a hunt for treasure. And this gives Major, Mother and Granny an idea – they will set up a special treasure hunt for the little ones. This leads to unexpected results and a very happy ending.

programme.title: BeddyByes
programme.desc: MeMo catches some colourful seed pods that fall from the Play Tree. At Play Time, MeMo throws a beach ball to BaBa and explains how to catch, but BaBa can’t do it. At Yummy Time, with eyes open and concentrating hard, BaBa eventually catches some seeds knocked over by MeMo. Fungi and Pungi play catch with the beach ball on the Lullaby Lake, and at Storytime, they catch a kiss blown by Gramma Leeba.

programme.title: In the Night Garden
programme.desc: In a magical forest, colourful characters have adventures. The Tombliboos ride on the Ninky Nonk - what a bouncy ride! The Ninky Nonk stops in some very lovely parts of the garden, and then the Ninky Nonk stops again. When the Tombliboos chase after the ball, the Ninky Nonk sets off without them! Unn, Ooo and Eee follow the Ninky Nonk home, and the ball comes to play with the Tombliboos.

programme.title: CBeebies Bedtime Stories
programme.desc: A story read by a special guest. Eddie Redmayne reads a story about a little girl who wonders which animal would make the best pet.

programme.desc: Comedy-drama series providing an honest, uplifting and heart-warming portrayal of teenagers from Liverpool.
